question: What is the medical term for the very first menstrual period in a young female?
explanation: Menarche is the term used to describe the onset of the first menstrual cycle during puberty. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T5#GNS121_U5_T5_h1)

question: Which part of the female reproductive system is primarily responsible for producing estrogen and progesterone?
explanation: The ovaries function as the main endocrine glands of the female reproductive system, synthesizing and releasing female sex hormones. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T5#GNS121_U5_T5_h1)

question: Which part of the brain acts as the master control center to start the menstrual cycle?
explanation: Think of the hypothalamus as the head office in the brain—it sends the very first signal (GnRH) to kick off the cycle! [learn more](GNS121_U5_T5#GNS121_U5_T5_h2)

question: What does follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) do in the ovaries?

options.A: It helps immature eggs inside the ovaries grow.
options.B: It causes the muscular wall of the uterus to contract strongly.
options.C: It immediately stops all blood flow to the endometrium.
options.D: It thickens the outer layer of the vaginal walls.

explanation: True to its name, FSH 'stimulates' the little follicles in the ovary so the eggs inside can grow and get ready for action. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T5#GNS121_U5_T5_h2)

question: In a standard 28-day menstrual cycle, around which day does ovulation usually happen?
explanation: Day 14 is the classic midpoint of a 28-day cycle where ovulation takes center stage. Easy to remember! [learn more](GNS121_U5_T5#GNS121_U5_T5_h3)

question: What is the main job of the corpus luteum during the second half of the cycle?

options.A: To lower body temperature and decrease metabolic rate
options.B: To secrete progesterone and keep the uterine lining thick
options.C: To trigger the immediate onset of menstrual bleeding
options.D: To release a new batch of immature eggs into the tubes

explanation: The corpus luteum acts like a temporary caretaker, pumping out progesterone to keep the womb cozy and ready in case a fertilized egg arrives. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T5#GNS121_U5_T5_h3)

question: Which hormone surge gives the final push to release an egg from the ovary?
explanation: An LH (luteinizing hormone) surge is the magic spark that triggers ovulation. Great nursing concept to keep in your back pocket! [learn more](GNS121_U5_T5#GNS121_U5_T5_h4)

question: Why does a woman sometimes notice light spotting right before her period starts?

options.A: A sudden drop in hormone levels causes the uterine lining to start breaking down.
options.B: The corpus luteum grows too large and presses against the uterine wall.
options.C: An excessive surge of follicle-stimulating hormone forces blood vessels to leak.
options.D: High levels of progesterone cause the cervix to dilate prematurely.

explanation: When estrogen and progesterone take a sudden dip, the uterine lining loses its support, leading to that little bit of early spotting. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T5#GNS121_U5_T5_h4)

question: How many days does normal menstrual bleeding usually last?
explanation: A normal period generally lasts anywhere from 3 to 7 days. Knowing this helps you reassure patients in the clinic! [learn more](GNS121_U5_T5#GNS121_U5_T5_h5)

question: Why do teenage girls often have irregular periods in the first few years after starting menstruation?

options.A: The uterus is physically too small to hold a normal amount of blood.
options.B: The brain-ovary communication loop is still maturing, leading to irregular ovulation.
options.C: Increased physical activity stops the pituitary gland from working.
options.D: Dietary changes completely block the action of estrogen in the body.

explanation: It takes time for the body's hormonal feedback system to find its rhythm after menarche, which is why irregular cycles are totally normal at first. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T5#GNS121_U5_T5_h5)

question: What is the medical term for menstrual periods that are abnormally heavy or prolonged?
explanation: Menorrhagia is the clinical term used when a woman experiences excessive blood loss or unusually long periods. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T5#GNS121_U5_T5_h6)

question: Which chemical in the body is mostly responsible for painful menstrual cramps?
explanation: Prostaglandins make the muscles of the uterus squeeze tightly, which causes those familiar cramps. (That's also why anti-inflammatory painkillers help so much!) [learn more](GNS121_U5_T5#GNS121_U5_T5_h6)

question: Why do nurses ask patients about how many pads or tampons they use when assessing heavy periods?

options.A: It reveals the exact day ovulation occurred during the previous month.
options.B: It determines whether the patient has reached early menopause.
options.C: It measures the exact size and muscular strength of the uterus.
options.D: It helps estimate the actual amount of blood lost.

explanation: Since everyone's definition of 'heavy' is different, counting pads gives you a practical, objective way to measure blood loss. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T5#GNS121_U5_T5_h7)

question: Which important nutrient should you encourage in the diet of a patient with heavy periods?
explanation: Losing a lot of blood means losing iron, which can lead to tiredness and anemia. Pushing iron-rich foods is a classic nursing intervention! [learn more](GNS121_U5_T5#GNS121_U5_T5_h7)
